title: OTE Meaning Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Understand ote meaning salary when converting hourly to annual pay. Learn about the 38-hour week, tax brackets, super guarantee, and casual loading.

faqs.q: What does OTE mean for salary?
faqs.a: OTE stands for ordinary time earnings. It is the amount you pay employees for their ordinary hours of work, including shift loadings, commissions, and casual loading. For super guarantee purposes, OTE is the base on which you calculate the 12% contribution. Overtime payments are not OTE unless ordinary hours are not clearly defined. Understanding ote meaning salary helps ensure you meet your super obligations correctly.

faqs.q: How is super guarantee calculated on a salary?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of an employee's ordinary time earnings (OTE), paid on top of their salary. For a full-time employee earning $80,000 per year, the employer must contribute $9,600 to super, provided the employee's OTE does not exceed the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Salary sacrificed amounts that would otherwise be OTE still count for super. Overtime payments are generally not OTE, so they do not attract super.

Under the Fair Work Ombudsman's guidance, casual loading is part of the minimum pay rate for casual employees and counts toward OTE for super guarantee. For example, a casual employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour receives a 25% loading, making their casual rate $33.05 per hour. The full $33.05 is OTE, and super is calculated on that amount.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia

When you're offered an hourly rate or a salary, it's natural to want to compare them on an annual basis. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman and most awards. The formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by hours per week, then by 52 weeks. This gives you an annual gross figure before tax, super, and any deductions.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. For a 38-hour week, that's $1,004.90 per week, or $52,269 per year. If you're a casual employee, you add 25% casual loading, making the rate $33.05 per hour, which works out to $1,255.90 per week and $65,306 per year. These figures are the starting point for understanding your take-home pay.

### Understanding the 38-Hour Week

Most awards and enterprise agreements set ordinary hours at 38 per week. When you use [the timesheet](/) on this site, we assume 38 hours unless you change it. This is the standard for full-time employees. Part-time or casual workers may have fewer or irregular hours, but the annual conversion still uses the same formula with their actual weekly hours.

It's important to note that annualised wages and salaries under awards must not be less than what the employee would have received under the award for the work performed. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that an annualised wage can cover penalties, overtime, allowances, and annual leave loading, but it must be reviewed every 12 months to ensure compliance.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for adults 21 and over. Award rates are often higher, and they vary by industry and classification. You can find specific rates using the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Calculator. For a casual employee, the minimum pay rate including casual loading is $33.05 per hour, which is the award-free rate.

When converting hourly to annual, always use the base rate for your classification. If you work under an award, your ordinary hours and penalty rates may differ. The annualised wage arrangement must be documented, including which entitlements are covered and the maximum penalty hours before extra payment is due.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of the minimum hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. This loading is part of ordinary time earnings (OTE) for super guarantee purposes. The Australian Taxation Office confirms that casual loading counts as OTE, so super is calculated on the loaded rate. For example, a casual on $33.05 per hour has super of 12% on that amount, paid on top.

Super guarantee is 12% of OTE, with a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year for 2026–27. This means if your annual OTE exceeds that cap, your employer only needs to pay super on the first $270,830. Super is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. From $18,201 to $45,000, you pay 15 cents per dollar over $18,200. From $45,001 to $135,000, it's 30 cents. From $135,001 to $190,000, it's 37 cents. Above $190,000, it's 45 cents. Additionally, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners.

For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage of $52,269, the tax would be approximately $6,617 plus Medicare of $1,045, leaving a take-home pay of around $44,607 per year, or $857 per week. This is an estimate and does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### OTE Meaning Salary for Super Guarantee

Understanding ote meaning salary is crucial for both employers and employees. OTE, or ordinary time earnings, is the base for super guarantee contributions. It includes your ordinary hours of work, shift loadings, commissions, and casual loading. Overtime payments are generally not OTE unless your ordinary hours are not clearly defined in your award or agreement. The ATO provides a detailed list of payments that are OTE, such as ordinary hours, shift penalties, and piece rates.

If you have a salary sacrifice arrangement, the sacrificed amount may still count as OTE if it would have been OTE if paid directly. For example, salary sacrificed to super is OTE, but salary sacrificed to other benefits like a car is not. This distinction affects how much super your employer must pay.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. The fortnightly figure is simply weekly pay multiplied by two, which is useful for budgeting if you're paid fortnightly.

Remember, the annual pay shown is an estimate based on the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, refer to our [reference tables](/data) for award rates and tax brackets, or our [pay guides](/blog) for industry-specific advice.
